questions.q: The editorial quotes the verse, “Corruption has appeared on land and sea because of the evil which men’s hands have done” (30:41). Where does it say the remedy must begin?
options: With waiting for nature to recover
Not quite. The article says: With the reform of the individual – each person answerable for his own way of living.
With the reform of the individual – each person answerable for his own way of living
Yes. A society is a group of individuals.
With new machines alone
Not quite. The article says: With the reform of the individual – each person answerable for his own way of living.
With moving to other lands
Not quite. The article says: With the reform of the individual – each person answerable for his own way of living.
questions.rationale: “It says that every individual holds accountability for their actions. It gives the formula of the reformation of an individual for the societal transformation.”

questions.q: At an international conference someone remarked that the Maulana was speaking less than the others. What did he answer?
options: That he was trying to be a good listener
Right. He was more in the habit of listening than of speaking.
That he was unwell
Not quite. The article says: That he was trying to be a good listener.
That he had nothing to say
Not quite. The article says: That he was trying to be a good listener.
That he did not know the language
Not quite. The article says: That he was trying to be a good listener.
questions.rationale: “When one of the participants commented on my not speaking as much as the others, I told him that I was trying to be a good listener.”

questions.q: Impressed by the patience and efficiency of airport staff, what did the Maulana conclude the world really needs?
options: Not a “better order” – it has all the order it needs – but food for the soul
Well read. Spiritual nourishment is what is lacking.
More languages on notice boards
Not quite. The article says: Not a “better order” – it has all the order it needs – but food for the soul.
Stricter rules for travellers
Not quite. The article says: Not a “better order” – it has all the order it needs – but food for the soul.
Faster aeroplanes
Not quite. The article says: Not a “better order” – it has all the order it needs – but food for the soul.
questions.rationale: “The world has got all the order that it needs. Rather, it is food for the soul which humankind stands in need.”

questions.q: What does the article give as the short “formula” for realization of God?
options: The less one questions, the more one realizes
Not quite. The article says: The more profound the thinking, the higher the degree of realization.
The more profound the thinking, the higher the degree of realization
Yes. Reflection on God’s words and creations.
The longer the life, the greater the realization
Not quite. The article says: The more profound the thinking, the higher the degree of realization.
The more one travels, the more one realizes
Not quite. The article says: The more profound the thinking, the higher the degree of realization.
questions.rationale: “The formula for God realization (Marifah) is in short ── the more profound the thinking, the higher the degree of realization.”

questions.q: The article takes the ordinary act of walking as an example. What is its point?
options: Walking is the best form of exercise
Not quite. The article says: Even walking depends on many things working together – gravity, air pressure, oxygen, sunlight – so that, reflected on, it leads to the Creator.
Walking should be done in silence
Not quite. The article says: Even walking depends on many things working together – gravity, air pressure, oxygen, sunlight – so that, reflected on, it leads to the Creator.
Walking is harder than it looks
Not quite. The article says: Even walking depends on many things working together – gravity, air pressure, oxygen, sunlight – so that, reflected on, it leads to the Creator.
Even walking depends on many things working together – gravity, air pressure, oxygen, sunlight – so that, reflected on, it leads to the Creator
Well reasoned. Everything becomes a source of realization.
questions.rationale: “Walking on the ground is apparently a simple thing, but it is an extraordinary event… when we reflect on all these things, it becomes the greatest means to the attainment of high Marifah.”

questions.q: Why are believers asked to visit Makkah at least once in a lifetime, according to the article?
options: So that they may see the desert
Not quite. The article says: So that they may re-enact and experience what the Prophet Abraham and his family went through in carrying out God’s plan.
So that they may meet their relatives
Not quite. The article says: So that they may re-enact and experience what the Prophet Abraham and his family went through in carrying out God’s plan.
So that they may re-enact and experience what the Prophet Abraham and his family went through in carrying out God’s plan
Correct. The place bears witness to that history.
So that they may trade with other nations
Not quite. The article says: So that they may re-enact and experience what the Prophet Abraham and his family went through in carrying out God’s plan.
questions.rationale: “Believers were then commanded in the Quran to visit this place at least once in their lifetime so that they can enact, experience what the Prophet Abraham and his progeny experienced in carrying out the plan of God.”

questions.q: Speed breakers and red lights remind a rider that the road is not his own. What does the article take from this for life?
options: This world has a Creator whose guidance must be followed, alertly, rather than one’s own wish
Yes. A moment of carelessness leads to an accident.
Rules are made only for the careless
Not quite. The article says: This world has a Creator whose guidance must be followed, alertly, rather than one’s own wish.
One should avoid travelling at all
Not quite. The article says: This world has a Creator whose guidance must be followed, alertly, rather than one’s own wish.
Life should be lived as fast as possible
Not quite. The article says: This world has a Creator whose guidance must be followed, alertly, rather than one’s own wish.
questions.rationale: “These things show that there is a creator of this world. Here you must follow the rules and guidance of the Creator instead of following your wish.”

questions.q: How did the Prophet describe “the best of you”?
options: The one who has the most followers
Not quite. The article says: The one whose goodness is hoped for, and from whose evil people are safe.
The one who speaks most often
Not quite. The article says: The one whose goodness is hoped for, and from whose evil people are safe.
The one whose goodness is hoped for, and from whose evil people are safe
Right. One can be sure in advance of receiving good from him.
The one who is never angry at heart
Not quite. The article says: The one whose goodness is hoped for, and from whose evil people are safe.
questions.rationale: “The best of you is the one whose goodness is hoped for, and people are safe from his evil.”

questions.q: A man asked the Prophet who would have the greatest reward among those who strive, fast, pray and give. What was the answer each time?
options: “The one who is seen by most people”
Not quite. The article says: “The one who remembers God most”.
“The one who began earliest”
Not quite. The article says: “The one who remembers God most”.
“The one who does the most”
Not quite. The article says: “The one who remembers God most”.
“The one who remembers God most”
Well read. Remembrance is the essence of all worship.
questions.rationale: “The Prophet gave the same reply to all his questions. ‘Those who remember God receive all the rewards.’”

questions.q: People were thrilled by the news of the first landing on the moon. What does the article ask us to learn from that?
options: To be as moved by the earth, the moon and the order between them – the work of God – as we are by the work of man
Exactly. Remembrance is “to change the target of one’s vision.”
To doubt what newspapers report
Not quite. The article says: To be as moved by the earth, the moon and the order between them – the work of God – as we are by the work of man.
To take no interest in science
Not quite. The article says: To be as moved by the earth, the moon and the order between them – the work of God – as we are by the work of man.
To follow the news more closely
Not quite. The article says: To be as moved by the earth, the moon and the order between them – the work of God – as we are by the work of man.
questions.rationale: “Dhikr is to change the target of one’s vision, to become excited at the work of God, as people normally become excited at the work of man.”
